skill.name: audio-transcriber
skill.description: Transcribe audio recordings into Markdown transcripts and optional meeting summaries using Whisper and LLM command-line tools.
skill.summary: Creates timestamped Markdown transcripts and optional meeting notes from audio files.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most markdown code-fence, placeholder URL, changelog, and example credential detections are false positives after context review. Confirmed issues involve automatic package installation, user-environment changes, and transcript processing through Claude or GitHub Copilot CLI. No prompt-injection attempt or covert malware intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Automatic dependency installation during script execution
remediation.suggestion: Remove import-time pip installation and require explicit user approval in a virtual environment or documented setup command.

remediation.issue: Transcript text may be sent to external LLM command-line tools
remediation.suggestion: Default to local-only transcription and ask for explicit consent before sending transcript content to Claude CLI or GitHub Copilot CLI.

remediation.issue: Installer can modify managed Python environments
remediation.suggestion: Avoid --break-system-packages, pin dependencies, and prefer venv or pipx installation instructions.
Clarify that the provided helper script outputs timestamped segments and does not fully implement speaker diarization.

static_findings.snippet: - **Timestamp-based File Naming** - Avoid overwriting previous transcriptions
- Now uses timestamp to prevent data loss

if python3 -m pip install tqdm rich --quiet 2>/dev/null; then

if python3 -c "import faster_whisper" 2>/dev/null || python3 -c "import whisper" 2>/dev/null; then

content.value_statement: Audio recordings are hard to review, search, and share after meetings or interviews. This skill converts recordings into timestamped Markdown transcripts and optional structured summaries.
actual_capabilities: Detects Faster-Whisper, Whisper, ffmpeg, Claude CLI, and GitHub Copilot CLI availability.
Transcribes local audio files and writes timestamped Markdown transcript files.
Adds segment timestamps, detected language, source filename, and processing date to output.
Can generate optional meeting notes or summaries through Claude CLI or GitHub Copilot CLI.
Includes an installer script for Python transcription dependencies and optional model download.
Provides an example shell workflow for basic transcription and Markdown report generation.
limitations: The helper scripts require Python and a local Whisper-compatible transcription engine.
Optional LLM summaries may send transcript content to Claude CLI or GitHub Copilot CLI.
Speaker labels are described in documentation but are not fully implemented in the helper script.
Large audio files can take significant local CPU time and disk space.

use_cases.title: Create Meeting Notes
use_cases.description: Turn team meeting recordings into searchable transcripts and optional action-oriented summaries.

use_cases.title: Document Research Interviews
use_cases.description: Produce timestamped transcripts from interview recordings for review, coding, and quotation checks.

use_cases.title: Archive Training Sessions
use_cases.description: Convert lectures or training recordings into Markdown notes that are easier to share and search.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Transcript
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner transcription of one local file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Transcribe this audio file to a Markdown transcript with timestamps: meeting.mp3

prompt_templates.title: Meeting Minutes
prompt_templates.scenario: Generate transcript plus structured meeting notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Transcribe team-sync.m4a and create meeting minutes with topics, decisions, and action items.

prompt_templates.title: Interview Summary
prompt_templates.scenario: Review an interview with a custom summary goal.
prompt_templates.prompt: Transcribe interview.wav. Summarize key themes, user pain points, and direct quotes that need review.

prompt_templates.title: Local-Only Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Transcribe client-call.mp3 locally only. Do not send the transcript to external LLM tools.

output_examples.input: A team meeting recording named team-sync.mp3.
output_examples.output: A Markdown transcript with metadata, timestamped segments, detected language, and optional meeting notes.

output_examples.input: A customer interview audio file with a request for themes and quotes.
output: A transcript organized by timestamped segments.
A concise summary of themes, pain points, and quotes for human review.

output_examples.input: A long lecture recording where only transcription is requested.
output_examples.output: A timestamped transcript file without an LLM-generated summary when external processing is declined.

best_practices: Use a virtual environment before running installer scripts or Python helpers.
Review privacy requirements before enabling Claude CLI or GitHub Copilot CLI summarization.
Keep original recordings available until the transcript and summary are checked.
anti_patterns: Do not process confidential recordings with external LLM tools without explicit approval.
Do not run installer scripts in a system Python environment without reviewing package changes.
Do not treat generated summaries as final records without human review.

faq.question: Does this skill work without cloud services?
faq.answer: Yes. Local transcription can run with Faster-Whisper or Whisper. Optional summaries use external CLI tools.

faq.question: Which audio formats are supported?
faq.answer: The documentation lists MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG, FLAC, WEBM, and MP4 when compatible tools are available.

faq.question: Can it create meeting minutes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can ask Claude CLI or GitHub Copilot CLI to create structured meeting notes from the transcript.

faq.question: Will it identify speakers automatically?
faq.answer: Speaker identification is described, but the provided helper script mainly outputs timestamped transcription segments.

faq.question: Does the installer change my system?
faq.answer: Yes. The installer can add Python packages and may use package managers for audio tools.

faq.question: Should I review the output?
faq.answer: Yes. Speech recognition and LLM summaries can contain errors, omissions, or incorrect action items.
